desc:
Count the ordered pairs of integers (x, y) with 1 ≤ x, y ≤ n whose greatest common divisor is 1. The pairs (1, 2) and (2, 1) count separately.

These are the lattice points that an observer at the origin can see inside the square, because no other lattice point lies between them and the origin on the same line.

n = 1 -> 1    ((1,1))
n = 2 -> 3    ((1,1), (1,2), (2,1))
n = 4 -> 11
hints: Count, for each x, how many y in the range are coprime to x. Then sum over x.
Euler's totient phi(x) counts the numbers from 1 to x that are coprime to x. Summing it over x gives the count for one half of the symmetric square.
Compute phi for all values up to n with a sieve: start with phi[i] = i and, for each prime p, multiply the entries at multiples of p by (1 - 1/p).
editorial: Let S = sum of phi(i) for i = 1..n. The value phi(i) counts the pairs (x, i) with 1 ≤ x ≤ i and gcd(x, i) = 1, because gcd(x, i) = gcd(i, x) and the pairs with x equal to i count only for i = 1. So S counts the coprime pairs with x ≤ y.
The square is symmetric under swapping x and y, and the only diagonal pair that is coprime is (1, 1). So the ordered count is 2S - 1.
The sieve starts with phi[i] = i. When i is still unchanged it is prime, and every multiple j of i gets phi[j] -= phi[j] // i. The total cost is O(n log log n).
